body_markdown:
Old cars have a certain draw for many of us, and vintage buildings can do the same. Combine the two and you may be able to create a space for celebrating history, while also making new memories. For the residents of Plainwell, Michigan, just such a place recently opened, and with any luck it might inspire other, similar restorations elsewhere.


Plainwell is a town of about 4000 located 10 miles North of Kalamazoo. The building at the center of the story is a paper mill that dates back to 1887 but which has sat dormant in Plainwell for more than 25 years.


It was last owned by the local government, which sought an appropriate buyer for the 255,000-square-foot facility. It found just the person in Darius Grigaliunas, a former Olympic swimmer who has become well-known in the classic car world. He saw the old mill as an opportunity—not necessarily just one to make money or build a business, but to create something that might have staying power, like the vintage and classic machines it now holds.


The Grigaliunas family bought the paper mill from the city for $1 based on their plans for the space, and this past weekend they held a grand opening. The building will now be known as the[Classic Auto Mill](https://classicautomill.com/) and will be a place for classic car storage, restoration, and sales. It is the second such operation the family has created,[the first of which](https://classicautofactory.com/) being the Classic Auto Factory, located in DeKalb, Illinois, just west of Chicago.


The tall ceilings, exposed brick, and general feel of being in another time seem to capture a lot of the emotions common for many of us when surrounded by old cars, and this makes the space something more than just an old building.


Finding the right place for an auto-related business can be tough, and so can reviving old spaces like this paper mill. But the Grigaliunas family may have hit a home run with the Classic Auto Mill, hopefully creating a place they find rewarding to own, but one that will also be a source of pride for the community.


A car show celebrated the Mill’s grand opening.
